observations.seen: No frame shows outdoor day. The frames show a golden backlit sunset, a pink dusk, a purple/orange sunset and a blue moonlit night. In the dusk and sunset frames the road surface goes nearly white-pink and flat, with little form shading on the tiles or edges. The character reads as evenly lit rather than shaped by a 3/4 key.

The runner casts one long soft shadow toward the camera. A second darker stripe also runs along the road center, which suggests a doubled shadow. The torii gates, lanterns, islands and dragon cast no visible shadows on the road or clouds. The road edge has a dark gradient band that reads as fake shading.

Reflections are almost absent. The road and clouds are matte, and the sky color does not pick up on the gates or lanterns. Only faint specular appears on the dragon scales and the character's arm guards.

The concept is strong: a stone sky-road with receding torii gates over a cloud sea, flanked by floating bonsai islands and a dragon. The set is sparse, though. The same small island mesh repeats, and lanterns are spaced uniformly. The cloud sea is a flat plane with noise blotches, and the night frame shows dark blobs on it that look like artifacts. The recipe's saturated greens and warm wood palette are missing.
Depth haze, a sun/moon glow halo and a starfield are present. In the first frame the haze is so dense that it washes out the midground and the gates.

The road tiles use drawn grid lines with no roughness or albedo variation. The cloud plane is a noisy 2D texture. The dragon's body is a smooth tube with a repeating band pattern. The character's cloth and skin look plausible but low-contrast.

The dragon head and character are reasonably detailed. The dragon's serpentine body becomes a primitive cylinder pipe that runs alongside the road. The floating islands are low-poly inverted cones with a single tree, and the torii gates are simple boxes.

A strong central vanishing point leads through the gate stack, and the dragon anchors the right side. The runner covers roughly 8-10% of the frame, below the 18-25% target. The large empty cloud areas on the left and bottom feel unused.
The camera is a low over-the-shoulder chase behind the runner, not the side-on follow the recipe expects. The FOV looks wider than 50. All four frames use an identical framing.
Bloom and haze are heavy in the first frame, softening the whole image. The dusk frames have clipped, low-contrast highlights on the road. No visible color grading ties the palettes together.

Only the first frame shows a HUD. It uses consistent dark panels with gold serif numerals, segmented spark/strain bars, a distance progress bar, a days-left badge and a centered title card. It is readable and on-theme. The title card sits over the gate focal area.
